original_question: Extend the action-angle theorem in a neighbourhood of a Liouville torus at singular points of the Poisson structure.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 5.1 in the PDF version: Extend the action-angle theorem in a neighbourhood of a Liouville torus at singular points of the Poisson structure.
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim. It correctly identifies the precise target as the local extension problem for action-angle coordinates near a Liouville torus in the Poisson setting, and it does not drift into the neighboring global-obstruction problem or the narrower splittable refinement.
missing_details: The ambient category is the smooth real Poisson category: a smooth Poisson manifold (M, Π) with smooth R-valued commuting functions, and angle coordinates valued in R/Z.

The paper's notion of an integrable system on a Poisson manifold should be stated: if M has dimension n and maximal Poisson rank 2r, then F = (f1, ..., fs) is Liouville integrable when the fi pairwise Poisson-commute, their differentials are independent on a dense open set, and r + s = n.

Liouville torus is not just any torus: in the regular theorem it is the compact integral manifold L_m of the Hamiltonian vector fields X_f1, ..., X_fs through m, and Theorem 5.2 concludes that L_m is a torus T^r.
The regular theorem being extended has explicit hypotheses that are implicit in your draft: df1 ∧ ... ∧ dfs(m) != 0, rank Π(m) = 2r, and the integral manifold L_m is compact.

To make the question stand-alone, one should state what extension is sought: an analogue of the local coordinates (θ1, ..., θr, σ1, ..., σs) near L_m, with U ≅ T^r x B^s, Π in the action-angle normal form sum_i ∂/∂θ_i ∧ ∂/∂σ_i, and σ_{r+1}, ..., σ_s serving as Casimir/transverse coordinates.
The phrase singular points of the Poisson structure should be unpacked as points where the Poisson structure is not regular, i.e. where the rank of Π drops or is not locally constant.

The nearby context adds an important caveat: in general there is no simultaneous splitting of the Poisson structure and the integrable system into symplectic-leaf and transverse parts; the paper therefore states a narrower follow-up problem for splittable systems, but that is separate from the main target.

No extra singularity class or transversality hypothesis belongs to Problem 5.1 itself; examples such as b-Poisson manifolds are mentioned only as motivating special cases where such an extension is already partially known.
refined_question: Let (M, Π) be a smooth Poisson manifold of dimension n and maximal rank 2r, and let F = (f1, ..., fs): M -> R^s be a Liouville integrable system on (M, Π), meaning that the fi pairwise Poisson-commute, are independent on a dense open set, and satisfy r + s = n. Theorem 5.2 gives, near a compact regular integral manifold L_m of X_f1, ..., X_fs through a point m with df1 ∧ ... ∧ dfs(m) != 0 and rank Π(m) = 2r, local action-angle/transverse coordinates (θ1, ..., θr, σ1, ..., σs) with θ_i in R/Z, U ≅ T^r x B^s, Π = sum_{i=1}^r (∂/∂θ_i) ∧ (∂/∂σ_i), and σ_{r+1}, ..., σ_s Casimir/transverse coordinates. Extend this action-angle theorem to a neighbourhood of a Liouville torus when the Poisson structure is singular at the relevant point(s), i.e. when Π is not regular there.
justification: The draft is already the exact official problem stated by the paper: Problem 5.1 on page 42. The nearby context in Section 5 defines integrable systems on Poisson manifolds and states the regular action-angle theorem (Theorem 5.2, pp. 41-42) whose local normal form is meant to be extended. The sentence immediately after Problem 5.1 explains the main obstruction: in general one cannot simultaneously split the Poisson structure and the integrable system, and this leads to the narrower Problem 5.2 for splittable systems. Therefore the nearest paper-faithful target is Problem 5.1 itself, with Theorem 5.2 supplying the precise hypotheses and the content of the desired extension.
